Learn about eligibility How do I apply? Learn how to apply How do I pay back my loan? Learn about payments What is the 504 loan program? The 504 loan program provides long-term, fixed rate financing for major fixed assets that promote business growth and job creation. Certified Development Companies (CDCs) are authorized by SBA to originate in collaboration with a senior lender a 504 loan, SBA’s community-based nonprofit partners who promote economic development within their communities. CDCs are certified and regulated by SBA. The maximum loan amount for a 504 loan is $5.5 million. Am I eligible? To be eligible for a 504 loan, your business must: Be an operating business Operate for profit Be located in the U.S. Be small under SBA size requirements Not be a type of ineligible business Other general eligibility standards include falling within SBA size guidelines, having qualified management expertise, a feasible business plan, good character and the ability to repay the loan. Loans cannot be made to businesses engaged in nonprofit, passive, or speculative activities.

The vision for these next-generation systems are to enable groundbreaking mobile applications requiring high-quality low-latency visual, tactile and audio telepresence, in addition to massive capacity (upwards of 1 000 times) and connectivity (billions of users and machines). Next generation mobile communications have begun harnessing available frequencies at millimeter wavelength (30 – 300 GHz), where high propagation loss can be recovered by high-power transmitters with tens to hundreds of antennas, commonly referred to as Massive-MIMO antennas. The greater the number of antennas, the higher the transmit power that can be achieved by combining the individual power of each antenna, a technique otherwise known as beamforming. Industry is already exploring the use of massive-MIMO antenna arrays that allow increased simultaneous transmission capacity; millimeter-wave spectrum to alleviate the spectrum crunch in current frequency bands; and ultra-dense networks to allow short-range, high-speed data transfer. A web search engine, like Google, often returns thousands of results for a simple query. For example, if you type the search term “jaguar” into Google, around 200 million results are returned. This makes it very difficult to browse or find relevant information, especially if the search term has multiple meanings. If we search for “jaguar”, we might be looking for information about the animal, the car, or the Jacksonville Jaguars football team. Clustering methods can be used to automatically group search results into categories, making it easier to find relavent results. This method is used in the search engines PolyMeta and Helioid, as well as on FirstGov.

Crawford began his career as a journeyman bookbinder on the third shift in the Bindery before transferring to first shift just a month later. Early on, he was eager to take on more challenging work and quickly set his sights on growth. “I looked around and decided I wanted to be the Superintendent of Binding,” Crawford said. Above: Crawford early in his career. That mindset helped define his career. Determined to keep moving forward, Crawford pursued more complex assignments, obtained a secret clearance to handle more sensitive work, and steadily advanced through the ranks. pages.text: 7 of Latin America's Unmissable Festivals | National Geographic By Daniel Stables Published August 26, 2026 This article was produced by National Geographic Traveller (UK). Festivals are woven into the fabric of life throughout Latin America — from the Bolivian Altiplano and the Peruvian Andes to the far reaches of Easter Island. They’re events where communities come together to celebrate faith, heritage and identity, often blending Indigenous traditions with influences brought by European colonisers centuries ago. And for travellers, they’re an opportunity to experience local culture at its most vivid. Streets fill with music and dance, as performers parade through cities, towns and village squares, while age-old rituals are brought to life before cheering crowds. Here are seven of the best. 1. Originally an Indigenous festival of the Uru people, it centred on a pilgrimage to the sacred mountains surrounding Oruro, where participants prayed for protection from deities associated with toads, lizards and snakes. When the Spanish arrived, they blended these traditions with Christian beliefs, gradually shaping the modern-day Oruro Carnival. Its centrepiece is the Diablada — the Dance of Devils — during which revellers don elaborate demonic masks and costumes. You have an agency and freedom that only intensifies the thrill. In some places you’ll be able to drive your vehicle independently within national parks and private game reserves, camping within their boundaries using the gear you’ve carried. The goal was to restore the democratically elected government of Guillermo Endara and arrest Noriega on drug trafficking charges. At the time, Operation Just Cause was the largest and most complex combat operation since the Vietnam War. Nearly 26,000 combat troops deployed, with just under half being from bases in the United States. Two dozen targets were attacked throughout the country, using a wide spectrum of tactical operations including Military Operations on Urbanized Terrain (MOUT), Air-Assault, Airborne, and Special Forces. Plus, the first supermoon of the year arrives just before Thanksgiving. An owl perches atop a cactus in Tucson, Arizona, beneath a moonless night sky. November’s new moon offers ideal conditions for stargazing, with darker skies making distant stars, galaxies, and nebulae easier to spot. Sean Parker By Stephanie Vermillion Published October 29, 2026 Not one, but three meteor showers could bring streaking fireballs to November’s night skies. If that’s not enough to whet your appetite, here’s another: The month will bring the first of three consecutive supermoons —a phenomenon skywatchers haven’t seen since January. Northern lights season remains in full swing. While the sun’s peak period of activity, solar maximum, is behind us, we’re still seeing impressive autumn displays—including a mid-latitude show in early October. There’s likely more where that came from as winter’s long dark hours begin, especially in far-north locales like Iceland and Norway . Here’s everything to watch for in November’s night sky, including tips on when and where to watch. pages.title: 8 Night Sky Events to See in October, From Fiery Meteors to a Vanishing Star Cluster | National Geographic
pages.description: This month brings two meteor showers, an eerie orange-tinted full moon, and one of the year’s last chances to glimpse the Milky Way’s luminous core.
pages.text: 8 Night Sky Events to See in October, From Fiery Meteors to a Vanishing Star Cluster | National Geographic SCIENCE NIGHT SKY GUIDE 8 Night Sky Events to See in October, From Fiery Meteors to a Vanishing Star Cluster This month brings two meteor showers, an eerie orange-tinted full moon, and one of the year’s last chances to glimpse the Milky Way’s luminous core. A long-exposure photograph captures stars appearing to streak across the night sky above Joshua Tree National Park in California. By Stephanie Vermillion Photographs by Sean Parker Published September 24, 2026 With streaking meteors and exceptional planet sightings, October provides plenty of reasons to stay up and stargaze. Two meteor showers punctuate the month: The Draconids peak beneath the dark skies of a nearly new moon, while the Orionids arrive later in October. Saturn also reaches opposition, when the planet appears at its biggest and brightest, creating an excellent opportunity to glimpse its famed rings. Meteor showers—and, now that autumn has arrived, the northern lights —are best viewed beneath dark skies away from light pollution . But all is not lost for urban sky-watchers; some of the month’s top spectacles, including planet sightings, are visible through city lights. You just need to know when and where to look. Saturn at opposition — October 4 Saturn will reach its closest point to Earth, known as its opposition, around 8 a.m. ET on Oct. 4.
